NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The engineering change to prevent or mitigate the failure is to implement a dual-pressure monitoring system with differential pressure analysis. Standard practice uses a single pressure sensor at the pump outlet to detect occlusions by measuring absolute pressure increases. Our mitigation departs by adding a second pressure sensor at the catheter midpoint and analyzing the pressure difference between sensors to detect developing occlusions before they reach the absolute pressure threshold. The closest existing practice is multi-point pressure monitoring in industrial fluid systems, but our innovation lies in using differential pressure analysis specifically for early detection of partial occlusions in flexible medical catheters, which directly addresses the slow leak and partial occlusion detection failure mode.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is that pressure drop (ΔP) across a partial occlusion follows the Hagen-Poiseuille equation: ΔP = (8μLQ)/(πr⁴), where μ is viscosity, L is occlusion length, Q is flow rate, and r is occlusion radius. A partial occlusion creates a pressure gradient along the catheter length. By measuring pressure at two points (Pump and Mid-catheter), the differential pressure (P_pump - P_mid) increases as occlusion develops, while absolute pressure may remain below threshold. For a 20% flow reduction (Q₂ = 0.8Q₁), the differential pressure increases by approximately 56% (1/0.8² - 1 = 0.5625), providing an early warning signal before absolute pressure triggers the alarm.

- 1 differential pressure analysis algorithm implemented in pump firmware (c)

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Implant insulin pump with standard and modified catheters in test bench that simulates partial occlusions using adjustable flow restriction. Create 20 test cases with gradual occlusions (10%, 20%, 30% flow reduction) and complete occlusions. Record time to detection and false alarms over 14-day simulated wear period.

Instruments: Test bench with precision flow meter, pressure sensors at pump and midpoint, data acquisition system, and reference occlusion detection device.

Pass/Fail Thresholds:
- Complete occlusion detection: ≤15 minutes (pass)
- Partial occlusion (≥20% flow reduction) detection: ≤2 hours (pass)
- Nuisance alarms: ≤1 per 14 days (pass)

Duration: 14 days continuous operation with occlusion events introduced at random intervals.

Kill Criterion: If any complete occlusion takes >15 minutes to detect, or any partial occlusion >2 hours, or >1 nuisance alarm in 14 days, the intervention fails.
